_note: Build page parts list. 'bought' is changed through the claim bot (site or Discord) and copied back here by pull request. cost = dollars for what we buy (or what it cost if on hand); null = not priced; approx = typical price, shown with ~. group picks the buy-list section. Run python3 tools/embed_build_parts.py after editing.

v1.name: V1: line follower
v1.how: Follows a tape line down the hallway, counts junction and door marks to know where it is, and stops at the chosen room.
v1.can: Room-to-room trips sent from the site. Stops for anything in front of it (single depth sensor). Physical E-stop.
v1.cant: Leave the tape, or recover if it loses count.

v2.name: V2: room scanner
v2.how: Drives the hallway like a real car (it steers; it can't spin in place). At stops, a roof turret sweeps a lidar to match the scan to the saved map, and the camera on the hood reads the room marker by the door to confirm where it is.
v2.can: Room-to-room trips from the site with no tape. Gyro heading. Stops for obstacles even without Wi-Fi (the lidar wags left and right while driving). Hazard lights when it stops for a person or parks. Stops instead of guessing when unsure. Physical E-stop.
v2.cant: See into rooms (one point at a time, about 8 m down the hall), recognize people specifically, or turn in place.
v2.catch: Permission to place room markers, and the parts fit confirmed.

parts.what: World's Littlest Waymo Jaguar I-PACE diecast. The body and glass; the base and wheels may be replaced.
parts.note: On hand: ordered Nov 1, 2026, $49.32 total, order complete (BJ bought it; Subir splitting; Dan said he'll cover it all if we finish). Outside 112 x 45.6 x 51.2 mm, about 1:42. Isabel is measuring the inside.

parts.what: 1/43 4WD mini RC drift car (Dingdongwu, on Amazon). Gives the drive motor, steering, gears, wheels and battery (check the battery has its own protection board).
parts.note: Ordered by Noah, arriving Fri 11/06. Steers with a front servo or a left/center/right coil, so it can't turn in place. Confirm on teardown.

parts.what: The car's brain. Runs the motors, steering, safety stop and the camera. Its camera sits on the hood, facing forward, on a small printed stand; the flat cable snakes through the hood vent.
parts.note: Seeed order Nov 5 had 2 boards and the camera ($51.42 total). Counted: one board ($13.99) plus its share of shipping and tax. The second board is for another project.

parts.what: The car's eyes for room markers: it reads the printed marker by each door so the car knows which room it's at, and the car stops instead of guessing if it can't read one. Autofocus and higher resolution than the Sense's stock camera. Sits on the hood. Comes with a heat sink.
parts.note: Same Seeed order as the S3 Sense. Counted: $12.99 plus its share of shipping and tax.

parts.what: Small driver (DRV8835 class) for the drive motor. The steering servo runs straight from the ESP32.
parts.note: DRV8833 on hand (BJ). Channel B steers if the donor's steering is a coil.

parts.what: Tiny slide switch plus a tether or pull-pin that cuts motor power without Wi-Fi.
parts.note: A mini toggle switch from BJ's stash works; a slide switch if space is tight.

parts.what: Small piezo sounder for Waymo-style chimes (a must) and 2 amber LEDs on one pin. No turn signals: the LEDs blink together as hazards when the car stops for a person or is parked.
parts.note: LEDs and resistors on hand; piezo to buy (packs run about $6). Counted: one piezo and two LEDs.

parts.what: Steadies the power when the motors start, so the ESP32 doesn't reset.
Fits inside the shell; normal hookup wire is too thick.
parts.note: A 30 AWG spool or kit is about $8; the car uses roughly 2 m. Counted: only that.

parts.what: Optional. Insulation between boards and the metal shell; the printed tray, electrical tape or hot glue do the same job.
parts.qty: About 0.6 m of 1 in + 0.5 m of 1/4 in
parts.note: Pack is 4 rolls x 33 m (1/8 to 1 in) for $10.99, ordered Nov 5, arriving Sat Nov 7. Only the tape the car uses is counted (about 1% of the pack); BJ keeps the rest.

parts.what: 3D printed chassis to hold the parts, the roof turret dome, and printed markers for the rooms. Also the turret adapter (servo horn to TF-Luna) and the small stand that holds the camera on the hood.
Used to measure motor start-up and stall current. A tool, so it is not counted in the car's cost.
parts.note: Shown for what was used; $0 toward the build.

parts.what: Gives the car its own Wi-Fi in the hallway if campus Wi-Fi blocks it.
parts.note: Use a phone hotspot; nothing to buy.

parts.what: Small reflectance sensor under the car to follow the tape.
parts.note: KY-033 line sensor and two IR sensors on hand (Noah), tested on an ESP32.
Needs building permission. A roll is about $8 for 55 m; a two-room route is roughly 20 m. Counted: only that.

parts.what: 8 x 8 zone time-of-flight sensor, 90 degree view, up to 3.5 m. Faces forward from the bumper to stop for obstacles. Takes the place of the planned VL53L1X.
parts.note: Bought by Subir; arrived. Carrier with its own 3.3 V regulator; header pins to solder. Runs from the XIAO's 3V3 on the shared I2C bus (D4/D5). Price without shipping.

parts.what: Single-point lidar, 0.2 to 8 m, 5 g. Rides the roof turret: the servo wags it left and right while driving to stop for obstacles, and sweeps a full arc at stops to scan the hallway. I2C mode, address 0x10.
parts.note: Delivered Nov 5. Replaces the VL53L7CX (decided 2026-11-05). Powered from the motor rail, not 3V3.

parts.what: GY-521 MPU-6050 board. Tracks the car's heading between scans and on turns. 3-pack; two spares.
parts.note: 3-pack $12.97, delivered Nov 5. Counted: one board. The other two are spares.

parts.what: Sweeps the TF-Luna from a printed roof dome, like a real Waymo's lidar. Sweeps back and forth rather than spinning, so no slip ring. Needs a printed adapter from the servo horn to the Luna, and a hole drilled in the roof for the servo and its wires.
parts.note: 2-pack of 2 g micro servos (3.7 to 5 V, JR connector), $17.59, ordered Nov 5, arriving Sat Nov 7. Counted: one servo; the other is a spare.
